## Abstract

Kabarak University Library (hereafter referred to as ‘Library’) was started from the first book on 23rd August 2002, in a small room (previously a classroom) and had only three pioneer staff. It later moved to a modern library building with a seating capacity of 1000 users and adequate office and shelf space. The building was named Daniel T. Arap Moi Library in honour of the Chancellor who graciously sponsored its construction. A newly constructed building in Nakuru City campus houses a branch library with a seating capacity of 500 users. Currently, the Library boasts of about 40,000 volumes of books, access to e-resources and 26 members of staff.

## Book Donation to Kabarak University Library from Prof. Sung Park and Mrs. Eun Park

The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Henry Kiplagat, recently received a generous donation of books to the Kabarak University Library from Prof. Sung Park and Mrs. Eun Park, American missionaries serving with Africa Gospel Outreach. The donation includes 4,140 volumes covering 3,627 titles across a wide range of disciplines.

The collection features titles in Theology, Biblical Studies, Interreligious Studies, Family Studies, and Church History. It also includes important works in Philosophy, Psychology, Counselling, Sociology, Contemporary Issues, and African Religions, among others.

Prof. Kiplagat expressed his gratitude, noting that this donation will greatly enhance the library s resources by providing up-to-date, high-quality materials to support teaching and research. He emphasized that a well-equipped library forms a strong foundation for students, staff, and the wider community to engage in meaningful scholarship.

Furthermore, the Vice-Chancellor highlighted that students in non-theological programs will also benefit, as these resources help foster a biblical worldview and promote the integration of faith and learning. This generous donation perfectly complements Kabarak University s commitment to education grounded in a biblical perspective.

## 1. Library OPAC Guide

Our library uses the Koha Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC). It lets you search the library's collection from any computer connected to the internet. This guide shows you how to:

1Access the library OPAC

2Do a simple or advanced search

3Interpret the results pages

4Create your own item lists

5Place a hold / reserve a document

6Access your personal account

7Access other library resources

### Searching for information resources

The OPAC helps you find an item when you know its author, title or subject. There are two ways to search: basic search and advanced search.

#### 🔍 Basic search

A search box sits in the top bar once you open the catalogue. The simple search is a keyword search: it finds records that contain your search terms in any field. You can also choose to search by Title, Author, Subject and more.

Results show the book's bibliographic details, its call number and its status (available, checked out, withdrawn, lost and so on).

#### 🎯 Advanced search

For a detailed search, click "Advanced search". It lets you combine keywords with the Boolean operators AND, OR and NOT to limit your results and find a specific item. Click the "More options" tab to continue.

### Boolean operators

AND

Narrows your results to records that contain all your search terms. It makes the search more specific.

accounting AND information AND systems

OR

Expands your search using similar terms, with results for each of the terms.

women OR gender OR development

NOT

Excludes a term from your results. This example finds "leadership" items but leaves out those about "logistics".

leadership NOT logistics
